title: Trash
explanation: Things you've already deleted. They still take up space until you empty the Trash in Finder (right-click the Trash in the Dock and choose Empty Trash).
label: review

title: Photos library
explanation: Your photo and video library. Manage it inside the Photos app (for example, delete large videos or turn on Optimize Mac Storage) rather than removing files here.
label: keep

title: Music library
explanation: Your Music app library. Manage songs and downloads inside the Music app.
label: keep

title: Music folder
explanation: Your music and the Music app's library. Manage it in the Music app; Freespan won't remove it.
label: keep

title: Movies folder
explanation: Your videos and projects from apps like iMovie and Final Cut. Review and remove videos yourself in Finder or in those apps.
label: keep

title: Zoom recordings
explanation: Meetings you recorded with Zoom. Freespan won't remove them; delete recordings you no longer need in Finder.
label: keep

title: Xcode build data (DerivedData)
explanation: Temporary build products and indexes Xcode creates for each project. Safe to remove; Xcode rebuilds them the next time you build, which just takes a little longer.
label: safe

title: Xcode archive
explanation: A saved build of an app you archived for the App Store or TestFlight. Keep archives of versions still in use, because you need them to read crash reports from those builds; older ones can go.
label: review

title: Device support files
explanation: Debugging symbols Xcode copied from an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch for one OS version. Safe to remove; Xcode copies them again the next time you connect a device running that version.
label: safe

title: SwiftUI preview data
explanation: Simulators and caches Xcode uses to show SwiftUI previews. Safe to remove; Xcode recreates them the next time you open a preview.
label: safe

title: Xcode documentation cache
explanation: Downloaded developer documentation. Safe to remove; Xcode downloads it again when you open the documentation window.
label: safe

title: Simulator caches
explanation: Cached data the iOS Simulator keeps to start up faster. Safe to remove; it's rebuilt automatically.
label: safe

title: Simulator device
explanation: One simulated iPhone, iPad or Watch, including the apps and data installed on it. Removing it erases that simulator; you can create a fresh one in Xcode any time.
label: review

title: Swift Package Manager cache
explanation: Downloaded copies of Swift packages. Safe to remove; they're downloaded again the next time a project resolves its packages.
label: safe

title: CocoaPods cache
explanation: Downloaded copies of CocoaPods libraries. Safe to remove; `pod install` downloads them again when needed.
label: safe

title: Homebrew downloads
explanation: Installer files Homebrew downloaded. Safe to remove; your installed tools keep working, and Homebrew re-downloads if it ever needs them.
label: safe

title: Yarn cache
explanation: Downloaded JavaScript packages kept by Yarn. Safe to remove; Yarn downloads them again on the next install.
label: safe

title: pnpm package store
explanation: Shared JavaScript packages kept by pnpm. Safe to remove; pnpm downloads them again on the next install.
label: safe

title: npm cache
explanation: Downloaded JavaScript packages kept by npm. Safe to remove; npm downloads them again on the next install.
label: safe

title: Bun cache
explanation: Downloaded JavaScript packages kept by Bun. Safe to remove; Bun downloads them again on the next install.
label: safe

title: Python pip cache
explanation: Downloaded Python packages kept by pip. Safe to remove; pip downloads them again when you install something.
label: safe

title: uv Python package cache
explanation: Python packages the uv tool downloaded. Safe to remove; uv downloads them again when a project needs them. Your Python environments share files with this cache, so clearing it can free less space than shown.
label: safe

title: Gradle cache
explanation: Downloaded Java/Android libraries and Gradle versions. Safe to remove; Gradle downloads them again on the next build.
label: safe

title: Rust crate cache
explanation: Downloaded Rust packages kept by Cargo. Safe to remove; Cargo downloads them again on the next build.
label: safe

title: Docker Desktop disk image
explanation: The virtual disk holding all your Docker images, containers and volumes. Removing it erases all of them; prefer Docker Desktop's own cleanup (Troubleshoot > Clean / Purge data or `docker system prune`).
label: review

title: node_modules folder
explanation: JavaScript packages installed for one project. Safe to remove; running `npm install` (or yarn/pnpm) in the project brings them back.
label: safe

title: Swift package build folder
explanation: Build products for a Swift package (its .build folder). Safe to remove; the next `swift build` or Xcode build recreates it.
label: safe

title: Mail attachment copies
explanation: Copies of attachments you opened from Mail. Safe to remove; the originals stay in your email and Mail re-downloads them when you open them again.
label: safe

title: App cache
explanation: Temporary files a Mac App Store app keeps to work faster. Safe to remove; the app rebuilds what it needs, though it may be a bit slower the first time.
label: safe

title: Code editor cache
explanation: Cached data and downloaded update files kept by VS Code or Cursor. Safe to remove; the editor rebuilds it, and your settings and extensions are not affected.
label: safe

title: Test browser downloads
explanation: Browsers downloaded by testing tools like Puppeteer or Playwright. Safe to remove; the tool downloads them again the next time it runs.
label: safe

title: Browser cache
explanation: Web pages, scripts and images Chrome, Edge, Brave or Arc saved so sites load faster. Safe to remove (best with the browser closed); it downloads them again as you browse. Bookmarks, passwords, history and open tabs aren't affected.
label: safe

title: Chrome on-device AI model
explanation: An AI model Chrome downloads to run features like writing help on your Mac. Removing it frees the space, but Chrome downloads it again while those AI features are turned on.
label: review

title: Google updater downloads
explanation: Update packages Google's background updater downloaded for Chrome and other Google apps. Safe to remove; it downloads what it needs for the next update.
label: safe

title: App web cache
explanation: Cached web content kept by apps built on web technology, such as Slack, Discord, Teams or Claude. Safe to remove (best with the app closed); the app rebuilds it, and your sign-in, settings and messages aren't affected.
label: safe

title: Spotify offline music
explanation: Songs and podcasts Spotify saved for offline listening, plus its streaming cache. Removing it frees the space, but anything you downloaded has to be downloaded again in Spotify.
label: review

title: JetBrains IDE caches
explanation: Indexes and caches from JetBrains IDEs such as IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm or WebStorm. Safe to remove; the IDE re-indexes your projects the next time you open them, which can take a few minutes.
label: safe

title: Android emulator system image
explanation: The Android system an emulator runs, for one Android version. Removing it frees the space, but emulators using that version won't start until you download it again in Android Studio's SDK Manager.
label: review

title: Ollama AI models
explanation: AI models you downloaded with Ollama. Removing this deletes every model; you can download the ones you need again with `ollama pull`. To remove just one, run `ollama rm <name>` in Terminal instead.
label: review

title: Hugging Face model downloads
explanation: AI models and datasets downloaded by Hugging Face tools (for example Python's transformers library). Removing them is fine if you don't need them offline; code that uses them downloads them again, which can take a while for large models.
label: review

title: Codex runtime downloads
explanation: Runtimes and dependencies the Codex coding tool downloaded to run code. Safe to remove; Codex downloads them again when it needs them.
label: safe

title: Ruby gem cache
explanation: Downloaded Ruby packages kept by RubyGems and Bundler. Safe to remove; they download again the next time you install.
label: safe

title: pre-commit hook environments
explanation: Tools the pre-commit framework installed to check your code before each commit. Safe to remove; pre-commit sets them up again on the next commit.
label: safe

title: Node.js build headers
explanation: Header files node-gyp downloaded to build native Node.js packages. Safe to remove; it downloads them again when a package needs building.
label: safe

title: Go build cache
explanation: Compiled pieces of Go programs kept to make builds faster. Safe to remove; Go rebuilds them on the next build (`go clean -cache` does the same).
label: safe

title: Bazel build cache
explanation: Build outputs and downloads kept by Bazel. Safe to remove; the next Bazel build recreates them, which takes longer the first time.
label: safe

title: Prisma engine downloads
explanation: Database engines the Prisma tool downloaded. Safe to remove; Prisma downloads them again when a project needs them.
label: safe

title: Electron downloads
explanation: Copies of Electron that JavaScript projects downloaded while installing. Safe to remove; they download again on the next install.
label: safe

title: TypeScript type downloads
explanation: Type definitions your code editor downloaded for JavaScript packages. Safe to remove; the editor downloads them again as needed.
label: safe

title: Tool cache: {name}
explanation: Data a command-line tool keeps. Usually safe to remove, but some tools store settings or downloads here.
label: review

title: App cache
explanation: Temporary files an app keeps to work faster. Safe to remove; the app rebuilds what it needs, though it may be a bit slower the first time.
label: safe

title: Logs
explanation: Diagnostic logs and crash reports written by apps. Safe to remove; apps start new logs as needed.
label: safe

title: Spotlight search index
explanation: Spotlight search index. macOS rebuilds it on its own; deleting it only makes search slow and incomplete for a while, so Freespan leaves it alone.
label: keep

title: Siri & Suggestions activity history
explanation: A record of how you use apps and devices that macOS keeps for Siri, Spotlight and widget suggestions (the Biome database). macOS trims it itself; deleting it only resets those suggestions.
label: keep

title: Siri & Apple Intelligence data
explanation: Models, settings and learned preferences macOS uses for Siri, Apple Intelligence and suggestions. macOS downloads and manages these itself; Freespan leaves them alone.
label: keep

title: macOS background service data
explanation: Data kept by macOS's own background services (in Daemon Containers). macOS manages it; Freespan leaves it alone.
label: keep

title: Mail messages
explanation: Your email and attachments as stored by the Mail app. Manage it inside Mail (delete old messages or big attachments); Freespan never removes it.
label: keep

title: Messages history
explanation: Your iMessage and text conversations and their attachments. To free space, remove large attachments in Messages (or System Settings > General > Storage); Freespan never removes them.
label: keep

title: Safari data
explanation: Safari's history, bookmarks, Reading List and website data. To free space, clear history or website data in Safari's settings.
label: keep

title: Calendar & Reminders data
explanation: Your calendars, events and reminders stored on this Mac. Manage them in Calendar and Reminders.
label: keep

title: Passwords & keys (Keychain)
explanation: Your saved passwords, certificates and keys. Never delete these; manage them in the Passwords app or Keychain Access.
label: keep

title: Account sign-in data
explanation: The internet accounts (iCloud, Google, Exchange, ...) and Apple ID services this Mac is signed in to. Manage them in System Settings > Internet Accounts.
label: keep

title: Cookies & website data
explanation: Cookies and stored website data for Apple's apps and services, which keep you signed in. Removing them signs you out of websites; clear them from Safari's settings instead.
label: keep

title: Apple app data
explanation: Settings, documents and data kept by apps and services that come with macOS (Notes, Photos, Mail, Siri and others). Manage it from inside those apps; Freespan leaves it alone. Caches inside it are listed separately.
label: keep

title: Saved window state
explanation: Window positions macOS restores when you reopen apps. It's small and macOS replaces it constantly, so Freespan leaves it alone.
label: keep

title: Unsaved document versions
explanation: Changes macOS saved automatically for documents you haven't saved yet. Deleting this can lose work; save or close those documents instead.
label: keep

title: macOS data
explanation: Data macOS keeps for itself in your Library folder (sharing, Home, Weather, status and follow-up services, metadata and similar). macOS manages it; Freespan leaves it alone.
label: keep

title: System-wide caches
explanation: Caches shared by all users and macOS services. They need administrator rights to change, so Freespan leaves them alone; macOS trims them itself.
label: protected

title: iPhone or iPad backup
explanation: A full backup of an iPhone or iPad made by Finder. Removing it is fine if the device is backed up to iCloud or you no longer need it; check the date first in Finder > your device > Manage Backups.
label: review

title: Installer or archive download
explanation: A disk image, installer package or archive you downloaded. Safe to remove if the app is already installed or you've already extracted what you needed.
label: review

title: Old download
explanation: Something you downloaded more than a month ago and haven't opened since. Move it somewhere permanent if you still need it; otherwise it can go.
label: review

title: Recent download
explanation: Something you downloaded or used in the last month, so you may still need it. Check it before removing.
label: review

title: Built-in Apple app
explanation: An app that ships with macOS. It's protected by the system and can't be removed.
label: protected

title: Application
explanation: An installed app. If you no longer use it, moving it to the Trash uninstalls it, and you can reinstall it later from the App Store or the developer's website.
label: review

title: Virtual memory & sleep image
explanation: Swap files macOS uses when memory is full, plus the sleep image saved when your Mac sleeps. macOS manages these itself; they shrink after a restart.
label: protected

title: System temporary files
explanation: Temporary files and caches for apps that are running. macOS cleans these up on its own, especially after a restart.
label: protected

title: macOS system data
explanation: Databases, logs and settings macOS needs to run. Protected; Freespan never touches them. Time Machine local snapshots also count as system data, and macOS deletes them automatically when space runs low.
label: protected

title: Shared system library
explanation: Fonts, drivers, frameworks and app support files shared by every user on this Mac. Protected; changing them needs administrator rights.
label: protected

title: macOS
explanation: The operating system itself and the command-line tools installed for all users. Protected; macOS and the Time Machine snapshots it keeps are managed by the system.
label: protected

title: Shared folder
explanation: Files shared between all accounts on this Mac (/Users/Shared). Some apps keep data here too. Freespan only cleans your own home folder.
label: protected

title: Other user: {name}
explanation: Files that belong to another account on this Mac. Freespan only cleans your own home folder; sign in as that user to clean theirs.
label: protected

title: Large, untouched file
explanation: A big file you haven't opened or changed in over six months. If you don't need it any more, removing it frees the space; consider moving it to an external drive or cloud storage instead.
label: review
